post.title: Margin calls explained with acorns: the math behind the call
post.ig:
Squirrel borrows acorns. Stock drops 33%. Lender wants them back.
Regulation T (Federal Reserve) lets a broker lend up to 50% of a stock's price to start. FINRA Rule 4210 requires equity of at least 25% of market value; many brokers ask 30% or more.
Our math: $5,000 cash + $5,000 loan buys $10,000 of stock. At 25% maintenance, the call hits at $6,666.67, a 33.3% drop. A 50% drop wipes out 100% of the $5,000 cash.
Brokers can sell without calling first. FINRA data: US margin debt was about $607B at end of 2022 and about $1.2T at end of 2025.
Sources: Federal Reserve (Regulation T), FINRA Rule 4210 and margin statistics, SEC, YCharts.
